lem-partial-negative-weight-crossing-tim:
## Statement

Let $M\ge0$, $\eta>0$, $L\ge0$, $\epsilon>0$, and let $w:[t_0,t_0+2M/\eta]\to[-M,0]$ and $\theta:[t_0,t_0+2M/\eta]\to\mathbb R^q$ be absolutely continuous until the first time $w$ reaches zero. Assume $w(t_0)\in[-M,0]$, $\theta(t_0)=\theta_0$, and, almost everywhere before the crossing,

$$w'(t)\ge\eta/2,\qquad q'(t)\le |w(t)|(\epsilon+Lq(t)),\qquad q(t)=|\theta(t)-\theta_0|.$$

Then $w$ reaches zero at some $\tau\le t_0+2M/\eta$. At the first such time,

$$q(\tau)\le \begin{cases}\dfrac{\epsilon}{L}\bigl(e^{LM^2/\eta}-1\bigr),&L>0,\\[4pt]\dfrac{\epsilon M^2}{\eta},&L=0.\end{cases}$$

Thus the crossing remains in $|\theta-\theta_0|<r_0$ whenever the displayed bound is less than $r_0$. The crossing-time bound depends on the initial negative-weight magnitude $M$.
lem-pushforward-support-is-closure-of-im:
## Statement

Let $X\subseteq\mathbb R^k$ and $Y\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be closed Euclidean subspaces. Let $\mu$ be a finite nonnegative Borel measure on $X$, define $\operatorname{spt}\mu=\{x:\mu(U)>0\text{ for every relatively open neighborhood }U\text{ of }x\}$, and let $f:X\to Y$ be continuous. Define the pushforward by $f_\#\mu(A)=\mu(f^{-1}(A))$ for Borel $A$. Then

$$\operatorname{spt}(f_\#\mu)=\overline{f(\operatorname{spt}\mu)}.$$
def-partial-one-homogeneous-measure-proj:
## Definition

Let $(\Theta,\mathcal T)$ be a measurable space and let $\mu$ be a finite nonnegative measure on $(\mathbb R\times\Theta,\mathcal B(\mathbb R)\otimes\mathcal T)$ such that $\int|w|d\mu(w,\theta)<\infty$. Set $w_+=\max(w,0)$ and $w_-=\max(-w,0)$, and define finite nonnegative measures on $\Theta$ by

$$\alpha_\mu(B)=\int_{\mathbb R\times B}w_+d\mu,\qquad\beta_\mu(B)=\int_{\mathbb R\times B}w_-d\mu\quad(B\in\mathcal T).$$

The partially one-homogeneous signed projection is

$$h^1(\mu)=\alpha_\mu-\beta_\mu,\qquad h^1(\mu)(B)=\int_{\mathbb R\times B}w\,d\mu(w,\theta).$$

It is a finite signed measure. For every bounded measurable $\varphi:\Theta\to\mathbb R$, define its integral against this signed projection by

$\int_\Theta\varphi\,dh^1(\mu):=\int_\Theta\varphi d\alpha_\mu-\int_\Theta\varphi d\beta_\mu=\int_{\mathbb R\times\Theta}w\varphi(\theta)d\mu(w,\theta).$

Put $\lambda_\mu=\alpha_\mu+\beta_\mu$, so $\lambda_\mu(B)=\int_{\mathbb R\times B}|w|d\mu$. Its total variation satisfies $|h^1(\mu)|(B)\le\lambda_\mu(B)$ for every $B\in\mathcal T$. Therefore $\int\widetilde Vd|h^1(\mu)|\le\int |w|\widetilde V(\theta)d\mu$ for every bounded nonnegative measurable $\widetilde V$.

If $\mathcal H$ is a separable real Hilbert space and $\varphi:\Theta\to\mathcal H$ is bounded and strongly measurable, then for every $z\in\mathcal H$ the feature moment satisfies $\langle z,\int w\varphi(\theta)d\mu\rangle=\int\langle z,\varphi(\theta)\rangle dh^1(\mu)$, with the scalar integral defined above. The raw measures $\alpha_\mu$ and $\beta_\mu$ record positive and negative parameter weights before cancellation and need not be mutually singular; for example, if $\mu$ assigns mass one to each of $(1,\theta_0)$ and $(-1,\theta_0)$ and zero elsewhere, then $\alpha_\mu=\beta_\mu$ both assign mass one to $\theta_0$ while $h^1(\mu)=0$. Thus the signed projection does not by itself determine a penalty of the form $\int|w|\widetilde V(\theta)d\mu$.
def-two-homogeneous-measure-projection:
## Definition

Let $d\ge2$, let $\mathbb S^{d-1}=\{\theta\in\mathbb R^d:|\theta|=1\}$, and let $\mu$ be a finite nonnegative Borel measure on $\mathbb R^d$ with $\int|u|^2d\mu(u)<\infty$. Define $\rho(u)=u/|u|$ for $u\ne0$. The **two-homogeneous projection** of $\mu$ is the set function on Borel $A\subseteq\mathbb S^{d-1}$

$$h^2(\mu)(A)=\int_{\mathbb R^d\setminus\{0\}}\mathbf1_A(\rho(u))|u|^2d\mu(u).$$

It is a finite nonnegative Borel measure: the integrand defines the weighted measure $|u|^2\mu$ on $\mathbb R^d\setminus\{0\}$, and preimages under the continuous map $\rho$ preserve disjoint unions; its total mass is at most $\int|u|^2d\mu$. Mass at $u=0$ contributes zero. If $\Phi$ or $V$ is positively two-homogeneous, this projection records its radial integral on the sphere; the exact identities are stated separately.
lem-bounded-domain-degree-properties:
## Statement

Let $d\ge1$, let $U\subset\mathbb R^d$ be bounded and open, and let $f:\overline U\to\mathbb R^d$ be continuous. For $y\notin f(\partial U)$, put $K=f^{-1}(\{y\})\cap U$ and define $D(f,U,y)$ by

$$f_*[U]_K=D(f,U,y)[\mathbb R^d]_{\{y\}}\quad\text{in }H_d(\mathbb R^d,\mathbb R^d\setminus\{y\};\mathbb Z),$$

where $[U]_K$ is the unique relative orientation class restricting to the standard local generator on $K$, and $[\mathbb R^d]_{\{y\}}$ is the positive local generator. This integer is well-defined. It is nonzero only if $f^{-1}(y)\cap U\ne\varnothing$, and $D(\operatorname{id},U,y)=1$ whenever $y\in U$. If $U_1,U_2\subset U$ are disjoint bounded open sets, $y\notin f(\partial U_i)$ for $i=1,2$, and every point of $f^{-1}(y)\cap U$ lies in $U_1\cup U_2$, then

$$\deg(f,U,y)=\deg(f,U_1,y)+\deg(f,U_2,y).$$

If $H:[0,1]\times\overline U\to\mathbb R^d$ and $y:[0,1]\to\mathbb R^d$ are continuous and $y(t)\notin H_t(\partial U)$ for every $t$, then $D(H_0,U,y(0))=D(H_1,U,y(1))$.
lem-feature-energy-continuous-under-w2-o:
## Statement

Assume the feature-energy hypotheses on a closed convex set $Q_r\subseteq\Omega$, and let $\mu_n,\mu\in\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d)$ be concentrated on $Q_r$, with finite feature energy and $W_2(\mu_n,\mu)\to0$. Then $F(\mu_n)\to F(\mu)$.
lem-mean-field-first-variation-and-measu:
## Statement

Let $\mathcal H$ be a real Hilbert space, let $\Omega$ be the feature domain, and let $F(\mu)=R(\int_\Omega\Phi\,d\mu)+\int_\Omega V\,d\mu$ be finite on a finite nonnegative Borel measure $\mu$, with $R$ differentiable and convex. Define $G_\mu(u)=dR_{m_\mu}[\Phi(u)]+V(u)$, where $m_\mu=\int_\Omega\Phi\,d\mu$. Then $\mu$ minimizes $F$ over all finite nonnegative Borel measures if and only if $G_\mu(u)\ge0$ for every $u\in\Omega$ and $G_\mu(u)=0$ for $\mu$-almost every $u$.
lem-partial-energy-continuous-under-w2:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^q$ be closed and convex, let $\varphi:\Theta\to\mathcal H$ and $\widetilde V:\Theta\to[0,\infty)$ be bounded Lipschitz maps, and set $\Phi(w,\theta)=w\varphi(\theta)$ and $V(w,\theta)=|w|\widetilde V(\theta)$. If $\mu_n,\mu\in\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R\times\Theta)$ and $W_2(\mu_n,\mu)\to0$, then $F(\mu_n)\to F(\mu)$.
lem-partial-feature-flow-moment-and-ener:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $\Theta$ be either all of $\mathbb R^q$ or the compact closure of a nonempty bounded convex Euclidean domain and let $\phi:\Theta\to H$ and $W:\Theta\to[0,\infty)$ be bounded $C^{1,1}$ maps, with $H$ separable Hilbert. Put $\Phi(w,\theta)=w\phi(\theta)$, $V(w,\theta)=|w|W(\theta)$, and assume the feature-energy hypotheses and the prescribed differentiable risk $R\ge0$. Let $\mu_t$ be any flow in the feature-energy Wasserstein definition. Write $m_t=\int w\phi(\theta)d\mu_t$, $f_t=\nabla R(m_t)$, $P_t=\int|w|W(\theta)d\mu_t$, $S(t)=\int w^2d\mu_t$ and $A(t)=\int|v_t|^2d\mu_t$. On every finite interval these quantities have continuous or absolutely continuous representatives as appropriate, and
$$F(\mu_t)-F(\mu_s)=-\int_s^t A(q)dq,\qquad S(t)-S(s)=-2\int_s^t(\langle f_q,m_q\rangle+P_q)dq.$$
These identities hold at every finite pair of endpoints. In particular $F(\mu_t)\le E_0:=F(\mu_0)<\infty$ and $\int_0^\infty A(t)dt\le E_0$. If $\sup_{t\ge0}\|m_t\|\le M$, then, with $D=\sup_{R(z)\le E_0}\|\nabla R(z)\|$,
$$0\le S(t)\le S(0)+2(DM+E_0)t.$$
No bounded-support assumption on the initial weights is required.
lem-partial-homogeneous-negative-level-t:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $\mathcal H$ be a real Hilbert space, let $q\ge1$, let $c\ge0$, and let $\varphi:\Theta\to\mathcal H$ be bounded and continuously differentiable with bounded Lipschitz differential. For $s\in\{-1,1\}$ and $f\in\mathcal H$ put
$$H_{s,f}(\theta)=s\langle f,\varphi(\theta)\rangle+c.$$
Assume one of the following alternatives. In the bounded alternative, $\Theta$ is the closure of a bounded nonempty open convex subset of $\mathbb R^q$ with $C^1$ boundary, and $\partial_nH_{s,f}=0$ on its boundary for every $f$. In the unbounded alternative, $\Theta=\mathbb R^q$ and, for every $f$, $H_{s,f}(r\cdot)$ has a limit $H_{s,f}^\infty$ uniformly in $C^1(\mathbb S^{q-1})$ as $r\to\infty$.

Fix $s,f_0$ and $a_0<0$. Suppose $H:=H_{s,f_0}$ has dense regular values in its range and, in the unbounded alternative, the same holds for $H^\infty:=H_{s,f_0}^\infty$. Values whose level sets are empty count as regular. There exist numbers $a,b$ and $\epsilon>0$ with
$$a_0<a<b<0$$
such that the following two assertions hold on every finite interval $[t_0,t_1]$. Let $f:[t_0,t_1]\to\mathcal H$ be Borel with $\|f(t)-f_0\|\le\epsilon$ for every $t$, and let $\rho:[t_0,t_1]\to(0,\infty)$ be continuous. Every absolutely continuous path $\theta:[t_0,t_1]\to\Theta$ satisfying
$$\dot\theta(t)=-\rho(t)\nabla H_{s,f(t)}(\theta(t))\quad\text{for almost every }t$$
and $H(\theta(t_0))\le a$ satisfies $H(\theta(t))<b$ for all $t$. Every absolutely continuous path satisfying the equation with the opposite sign and $H(\theta(t_1))\le a$ satisfies $H(\theta(t))<b$ throughout the same interval. The constants do not depend on the interval, on $\rho$, or on the order in which the forcing values occur. In particular they apply after reversing time and reversing the forcing path. By decreasing $\epsilon$ if necessary, one also has $H_{s,f(t)}(\theta)\le b/2<0$ whenever $H(\theta)<b$.
lem-partial-homogeneous-penalty-is-const:
## Statement

Let $W:\Theta\to[0,\infty)$ be bounded and $C^1$, and suppose $V(w,\theta)=|w|W(\theta)$ is globally $\lambda$-semiconvex on $\mathbb R\times\Theta$ for one finite coefficient $\lambda$. Suppose either $\Theta=\mathbb R^q$, or $\Theta$ is the closure of a nonempty bounded connected open convex set with $C^1$ boundary and $dW(n)=0$ on that boundary. Then $W\equiv c$ for some $c\ge0$. In the full partial-model hypotheses, the Neumann assumption for $G_f=\langle f,\varphi\rangle+W$ at $f=0$ supplies the latter condition. Consequently, writing $H_+=\langle f,\varphi\rangle+c$ and $H_-=-\langle f,\varphi\rangle+c$, one has $H_-=2c-H_+$ and $\nabla H_-=-\nabla H_+$.
lem-signed-narrow-convergence-controls-b:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $X$ be a nonempty closed subset of $\mathbb R^k$ and let $\sigma_n,\nu$ be finite signed Borel measures on $X$, with $\int f d\sigma_n\to\int f d\nu$ for every bounded continuous real function $f$ on $X$. Then their total variations have uniformly bounded masses and are uniformly tight. For every bounded norm-continuous map $\phi:X\to H$ into a separable real Hilbert space,
$$\left\|\int\phi d\sigma_n-\int\phi d\nu\right\|_H\longrightarrow0.$$
Also $\|\sigma_n-\nu\|_{BL}\to0$, where the bounded-Lipschitz norm uses $\|f\|_\infty+\operatorname{Lip}(f)\le1$. For every nonnegative $\psi\in C_c(X)$ and bounded nonnegative continuous $W$ on $X$,
$$\int\psi d\nu^+\le\liminf_n\int\psi d\sigma_n^+,\qquad \int Wd|\nu|\le\liminf_n\int Wd|\sigma_n|.$$
Signed Bochner integrals mean the difference of the two Jordan-part integrals. The same conclusions about moments and BL convergence hold as $t\to\infty$ for a narrowly convergent continuous-time family, by the sequential criterion. Here narrow convergence explicitly means convergence against every function in $C_b(X)$, not merely compactly supported tests.
def-bounded-domain-degree-from-relative-:
## Definition

Let $d\ge1$, let $U\subset\mathbb R^d$ be bounded and open, and let $f:\overline U\to\mathbb R^d$ be continuous. For $y\notin f(\partial U)$ the set $K=f^{-1}(\{y\})\cap U$ is compact in $U$: its closure preimage is closed in the compact set $\overline U$ and avoids $\partial U$. Give $U$ its standard orientation. Let $[U]_K\in H_d(U,U\setminus K;\mathbb Z)$ be the unique relative orientation class restricting to the standard local orientation generator at each $x\in K$; for $K=\varnothing$ use the zero class. Let $[\mathbb R^d]_{\{y\}}$ be the positive generator of $H_d(\mathbb R^d,\mathbb R^d\setminus\{y\};\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$. The bounded-domain degree is the integer $\deg(f,U,y)$ determined by

$$f_*[U]_K=\deg(f,U,y)[\mathbb R^d]_{\{y\}},$$

where $f$ is regarded as a map of pairs $(U,U\setminus K)\to(\mathbb R^d,\mathbb R^d\setminus\{y\})$. The following local lemma proves that this definition is well-defined and has the required normalization, additivity, and moving-target homotopy properties.
def-one-hidden-layer-particle-measure-mo:
## Definition

Assume AC for the flow clause below. Let $(\mathsf X,\mathcal A,\rho_X)$ be an input probability space, let $\mathcal H=L^2(\rho_X)$, let $\sigma:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be measurable, and put $\Theta=\mathbb R^{p+1}$ for hidden affine parameters $\theta=(w,b)$. Assume $\phi_\theta(x)=\sigma(w\cdot x+b)$ belongs to $\mathcal H$ for each $\theta$. On $\Omega=\mathbb R\times\Theta$, define the feature map $\Phi(a,w,b)=a\phi_{(w,b)}\in\mathcal H$. For a finite nonnegative Borel measure $\mu$ on $\Omega$ for which the Bochner integral exists, its particle-measure predictor is

$$f_\mu=\int_\Omega \Phi(u)\,d\mu(u)\in\mathcal H.$$

The corresponding objective is $F(\mu)=R(f_\mu)+\int_\Omega V\,d\mu$, whenever the scalar integral is finite, with $R:\mathcal H\to[0,\infty)$ a risk functional and $V:\Omega\to[0,\infty)$ a regularizer. For the empirical particle law defined on measurable $A\subseteq\Omega$ by $\mu_m(A)=m^{-1}\#\{j:(m a_j,w_j,b_j)\in A\}$, one has $f_{\mu_m}(x)=\sum_{j=1}^m a_j\sigma(w_j\cdot x+b_j)$, so a finite one-hidden-layer network is a particle-measure predictor (with an optional constant output bias added separately). A feature-energy Wasserstein gradient flow means an $AC^2_{\rm loc}$ curve of probability measures satisfying the finite-action continuity equation with Borel velocity equal almost everywhere to the negative minimum-norm element of the constrained subdifferential of the first-variation potential. This is the earlier model-flow definition; no existence or uniqueness follows from this definition. The flow use below requires all of the feature-energy regularity hypotheses. In particular, the classical ReLU feature map is not asserted here to meet those hypotheses merely because it is positively homogeneous.

def-signed-square-relu-feature-map:
## Definition

Let $d\ge2$, let $\rho_X$ be a Borel probability measure on $\mathbb R^{d-1}$ with finite second moment, and define $s(t)=t|t|$ and $\sigma(t)=\max(t,0)$. For $\theta=(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_d)\in\mathbb R^d$, define the signed-square ReLU feature in $L^2(\rho_X)$ by

$$\Phi(\theta)(x)=\sigma\!\left(\sum_{j=1}^{d-1}s(\theta_j)x_j+s(\theta_d)\right).$$

The two-copy parameterization uses this feature on one copy of $\mathbb R^d$ and its negative on the other copy; nonnegative measures on the disjoint union represent signed linear combinations of these features. The scalar signed-square map is continuously differentiable with derivative $s'(t)=2|t|$. This definition asserts differentiability of the resulting $L^2$ feature map only when its data law has the additional regularity needed for that conclusion; it does not assert that its differential is locally Lipschitz.
lem-flow-preserves-spherical-separation:
## Statement

Assume AC, the full feature-energy hypotheses on $\Omega=\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, and positive two-homogeneity of $\Phi$ and $V$. Let $\mu_t$ be the resulting Wasserstein gradient flow on $[0,T]$. If $K=\operatorname{spt}\mu_0$ is compact, is contained in $B(0,r_b)$, and separates $r_a\mathbb S^{d-1}$ from $r_b\mathbb S^{d-1}$ for $0<r_a<r_b$, then for every $t\in[0,T]$ the support $\operatorname{spt}\mu_t$ separates $r'_a\mathbb S^{d-1}$ from $r'_b\mathbb S^{d-1}$ for some $0<r'_a<r'_b$ depending on the flow and $T$. Here separation means that every continuous path with endpoints on the two spheres intersects the stated support.
lem-mean-field-projection-identities:
## Statement

For a finite nonnegative Borel measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb R^d$ with finite second moment, suppose $\Phi$ and $V$ are continuous and positively two-homogeneous, with $\Phi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathcal H$ taking values in a Hilbert space and $V:\mathbb R^d\to[0,\infty)$. Then

$$\int_{\mathbb R^d}\Phi(u)d\mu(u)=\int_{\mathbb S^{d-1}}\Phi(\theta)dh^2(\mu)(\theta),\qquad\int_{\mathbb R^d}V(u)d\mu(u)=\int_{\mathbb S^{d-1}}V(\theta)dh^2(\mu)(\theta).$$

If $h^2(\mu_n)$ converges weakly as finite measures on the compact sphere to $\nu$, then the feature integrals converge in Hilbert norm, the regularizer integrals converge, and $F(\mu_n)\to R(\int\Phi d\nu)+\int Vd\nu$. In the partially one-homogeneous model $\Omega=\mathbb R\times\Theta$, $\Phi(w,\theta)=w\varphi(\theta)$ and $V(w,\theta)=|w|\widetilde V(\theta)$ with bounded nonnegative $\widetilde V$, for every $z\in\mathcal H$ the exact feature identity is $\langle z,\int w\varphi(\theta)d\mu\rangle=\int\langle z,\varphi(\theta)\rangle dh^1(\mu)$, using the scalar pairing defined in the partial projection, and the penalty inequality is $\int|w|\widetilde V(\theta)d\mu\ge\int\widetilde Vdh^1(\mu)$. Weak convergence of signed $h^1(\mu_n)$ against all bounded continuous tests gives weak convergence of feature moments when $\varphi$ is bounded continuous. If AC holds, $\Theta$ is a closed Euclidean subset and $\varphi$ is bounded norm-continuous into a separable Hilbert space, it also gives Hilbert-norm convergence. Signed projection convergence alone does not imply penalty or full energy convergence for arbitrary lifts.
lem-w2-convergence-implies-homogeneous-p:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $\mu_n,\mu\in\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d)$, with $W_2(\mu_n,\mu)\to0$. Then $h^2(\mu_n)$ converges weakly as finite measures on $\mathbb S^{d-1}$ to $h^2(\mu)$. More generally, if $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^q$ is closed and $\mu_n,\mu\in\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R\times\Theta)$ converge in W2, with first coordinate $w\in\mathbb R$, then $h^1(\mu_n)$ converges weakly as finite signed measures against every bounded continuous test on $\Theta$ to $h^1(\mu)$.
thm-mean-field-particle-time-limits-inte:
## Statement

Assume AC and the feature-energy hypotheses. Let $\mu_t$ be a Wasserstein gradient flow from $\mu_0$ concentrated on a common cutoff $Q_{r_0}$, with $F(\mu_t)\to F^*:=\inf_{\lambda\ge0}F(\lambda)$. For each $m\ge1$, let $\mu_{m,t}$ be a finite-particle gradient flow for the same objective, with $\mu_{m,0}$ concentrated on $Q_{r_0}$ and $W_2(\mu_{m,0},\mu_0)\to0$. Assume that for every fixed $t$, $W_2(\mu_{m,t},\mu_t)\to0$ as $m\to\infty$, with both laws concentrated on a common cutoff for that finite time. Then both iterated limits exist and

$$\lim_{t\to\infty}\lim_{m\to\infty}F(\mu_{m,t})=\lim_{m\to\infty}\lim_{t\to\infty}F(\mu_{m,t})=F^*.$$

This is qualitative and gives no rate uniform in $m$ or $t$.
lem-flow-preserves-box-separation:
## Statement

Assume AC, the partially one-homogeneous feature-energy hypotheses on $\Omega=\mathbb R\times\Theta$, and $\Phi(w,\theta)=w\varphi(\theta)$, $V(w,\theta)=|w|\widetilde V(\theta)$ with bounded $C^{1,1}$ feature and penalty maps. In the bounded branch, let $\Theta$ be the closure of a nonempty bounded connected open convex set with $C^1$ boundary and assume $dG_f(\theta)[n_\theta]=0$ for every $f\in\mathcal H$ and $G_f(\theta)=\langle f,\varphi(\theta)\rangle+\widetilde V(\theta)$ and $\theta\in\partial\Theta$. In the unbounded branch, let $\Theta=\mathbb R^{d-1}$ and assume for every $f\in\mathcal H$ that $G_f(r\omega)$ has a uniform $C^1(\mathbb S^{d-2})$ limit as $r\to\infty$, with the dense-regular-value property required by the model. Let $\mu_t$ be the Wasserstein gradient flow from a law whose closed support $K_0$ is contained in $[-r_0,r_0]\times\Theta$ and separates the faces $\{-r_0\}\times\Theta$ and $\{r_0\}\times\Theta$. For every finite $T$, there is $\alpha>r_0$ such that $\operatorname{spt}\mu_t$ is contained in $[-\alpha,\alpha]\times\Theta$ and separates $\{-\alpha\}\times\Theta$ from $\{\alpha\}\times\Theta$ for every $t\in[0,T]$.
lem-partial-homogeneous-escape-from-nono:
## Statement

Assume AC, a separable real Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, and the feature-energy hypotheses: $R$ is convex and differentiable with locally Lipschitz differential bounded on sublevels, $\Phi$ is Fr\acute{e}chet differentiable, $V$ is semiconvex, and the nested cutoff sets and derivative-growth bounds in the feature-energy definition hold. Let $d\ge2$, $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^{d-1}$, $\varphi:\Theta\to\mathcal H$ be bounded and continuously differentiable with Lipschitz differential, and $\widetilde V:\Theta\to[0,\infty)$ be bounded and continuously differentiable with Lipschitz differential; set $\Phi(w,\theta)=w\varphi(\theta)$ and $V(w,\theta)=|w|\widetilde V(\theta)$. For every $f\in\mathcal H$, require dense regular values for $G_f(\theta)=\langle f,\varphi(\theta)\rangle+\widetilde V(\theta)$. Retain either (i) $\Theta$ is the closure of a nonempty bounded connected open convex set with $C^1$ boundary and $dG_f(\theta)[n_\theta]=0$ on $\partial\Theta$ for every $f\in\mathcal H$, or (ii) $\Theta=\mathbb R^{d-1}$ and for every $f\in\mathcal H$, $G_f(r\cdot)$ converges uniformly in $C^1(\mathbb S^{d-2})$ to a limit with dense regular values as $r\to\infty$. Let $\nu$ be a finite signed projection with nonoptimal relaxed objective $J(\nu)$, set $m_\nu=\int\varphi d\nu$ by the signed Bochner-integral convention in the relaxed-objective definition, and define $G_+(\theta)=dR_{m_\nu}[\varphi(\theta)]+\widetilde V(\theta)$ and $G_-(\theta)=-dR_{m_\nu}[\varphi(\theta)]+\widetilde V(\theta)$. Assume at least one of $G_+,G_-$ is negative somewhere, as is necessary for a nonempty negative cone. Let $I\subseteq\{+,-\}$ be the nonempty set of signs with a negative value, choose a negative regular level $-\eta_s$ for each $s\in I$, and put $K_s=\{G_s\le-\eta_s\}$ for $s\in I$ and $K_s=\varnothing$ otherwise. For a finite signed measure $\sigma$ on $\Theta$, define

$$\|\sigma\|_{BL(\Theta)}:=\sup\left\{\left|\int f d\sigma\right|:f:\Theta\to\mathbb R,\ \|f\|_\infty+\operatorname{Lip}(f)\le1\right\},$$

where $\|f\|_\infty:=\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}|f(\theta)|$ and $\operatorname{Lip}(f):=\sup_{\theta\ne\theta'}|f(\theta)-f(\theta')|/|\theta-\theta'|$ for Euclidean distance, taking $0$ when there are no distinct points. Set $A=(\mathbb R_{>0}\times K_+)\cup(\mathbb R_{<0}\times K_-)$. There is $\epsilon>0$ such that if $\|h^1(\mu_{t_0})-\nu\|_{BL(\Theta)}<\epsilon$ and $\mu_{t_0}(A)>0$ for a Wasserstein gradient flow $\mu_t$, then for some $t_1>t_0$,

$$\|h^1(\mu_{t_1})-\nu\|_{BL(\Theta)}\ge\epsilon.$$

The statement retains both sign branches and both source boundary alternatives.
lem-partial-homogeneous-projection-limit:
## Statement

Assume AC, a separable real Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, and the feature-energy hypotheses: $R$ is convex and differentiable with locally Lipschitz differential bounded on sublevels, $\Phi$ is Fr\acute{e}chet differentiable, $V$ is semiconvex, and the nested cutoff sets and derivative-growth bounds in the feature-energy definition hold.
